Container.Name: strawberry-notes
Container.Overview:
Self-hosted, MIT-licensed, multi-user, AI-native rich-text notes app. TipTap editor, [[wiki-link]] backlinks, semantic search over any OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint, full-workspace ZIP export, a Chrome/Firefox web clipper, and a first-class MCP endpoint.
Requires a Postgres 16+ database with the `pgvector` extension. Use the pgvector/pgvector:pg16 image (drop-in for postgres:16) if your existing Postgres doesn't have pgvector installed.
First-time setup (no shell commands needed): 1. Create a database and user for Strawberry on your Postgres. 2. Fill in DATABASE_URL below. Leave AUTH_SECRET blank — one is generated for you on first boot and kept in the Uploads path. 3. Start the container, open its log (Docker tab → strawberry-notes → Logs), and copy the setup code printed there. 4. Visit the WebUI — you'll land on a one-time setup page. Enter the code to create your admin account.
Docs: https://github.com/straplocked/strawberry-notes/tree/main/docs
Container.Requires: A Postgres 16+ database with pgvector. The DATABASE_URL field accepts the standard `postgres://user:pass@host:5432/db` shape.

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: Host port the WebUI is published on. Default: 3200.

Config.Name: DATABASE_URL
Config.Description: Full Postgres connection string. The user must own the target database; Strawberry will run migrations on first boot. Requires the pgvector extension.

Config.Name: AUTH_SECRET
Config.Description: 32+ bytes of base64 entropy used to sign session cookies. Leave blank — one is generated automatically on first boot and stored under the Uploads path below, so it survives container recreates. Only set this yourself if you need a stable value independent of that path (e.g. restoring onto a fresh volume).

Config.Name: AUTH_URL
Config.Description: Public URL where Strawberry is reachable, e.g. https://notes.example.com. Leave blank for LAN access; set explicitly when behind a TLS-terminating proxy that strips X-Forwarded-* headers.

Config.Name: ALLOW_PUBLIC_SIGNUP
Config.Description: Leave `false`. The very first admin account is created through a one-time setup-code flow at first boot (code printed in this container's log) — no need to open public signup for that. Set to `true` only if you want an instance strangers can register on afterwards.

Config.Name: Uploads
Config.Description: Where uploaded images live on disk. Survives container recreates.

Config.Name: MAX_UPLOAD_MB
Config.Description: Per-file upload size cap in megabytes.

Config.Name: REQUIRE_EMAIL_CONFIRMATION
Config.Description: When true, signup creates accounts unconfirmed and emails a confirmation link. Implies SMTP must be configured below.

Config.Name: SMTP_HOST
Config.Description: SMTP relay hostname for password-reset and notification emails. Leave blank to disable email entirely.

Config.Name: SMTP_PORT
Config.Description: SMTP port. 587 (STARTTLS) is most common; 465 with SMTP_SECURE=true for implicit TLS.

Config.Name: SMTP_USER
Config.Description: Optional SMTP auth username.

Config.Name: SMTP_PASS
Config.Description: Optional SMTP auth password.

Config.Name: SMTP_FROM
Config.Description: From: address on outbound mail. Required when SMTP_HOST is set.

Config.Name: SMTP_SECURE
Config.Description: `true` forces implicit TLS at connect time (port 465 deployments).

Config.Name: EMBEDDING_ENDPOINT
Config.Description: OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint (`/v1`). Leave blank to disable semantic search; everything else still works.

Config.Name: EMBEDDING_MODEL
Config.Description: Model id. Stick to a 1024-dim model to match the default EMBEDDING_DIMS below with zero extra config — e.g. qwen3-embedding:0.6b or mxbai-embed-large (Ollama), or text-embedding-3-small pinned to 1024 dims via the OpenAI API's `dimensions` param.

Config.Name: EMBEDDING_API_KEY
Config.Description: Bearer token for the embeddings provider. Optional for local providers like Ollama.

Config.Name: EMBEDDING_DIMS
Config.Description: Vector dimension. MUST match the provider's output dim. Default 1024 — pick a 1024-dim model above and leave this alone; changing it is a destructive re-embed.

Config.Name: PASSWORD_AUTH
Config.Description: Email/password sign-in. Set to `false` for OIDC-only or proxy-only deployments.

Config.Name: TOTP_ENABLED
Config.Description: Enable per-user TOTP/2FA enrollment from Settings → Security.

Config.Name: OIDC_ENABLED
Config.Description: Enable OIDC SSO. Requires the four OIDC_* fields below.

Config.Name: OIDC_ISSUER
Config.Description: OIDC issuer URL, e.g. https://auth.example.com/application/o/strawberry/

Config.Name: OIDC_CLIENT_ID
Config.Description: OIDC client id.

Config.Name: OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET
Config.Description: OIDC client secret.

Config.Name: OIDC_NAME
Config.Description: Label for the SSO sign-in button on /login.

Config.Name: OIDC_AUTO_PROVISION
Config.Description: JIT-create local users on first OIDC sign-in (requires the IdP to set email_verified=true).

Config.Name: OIDC_TRUST_EMAIL_FOR_LINKING
Config.Description: DANGER: auto-link OIDC sign-ins to existing email-matching local users. Account-takeover risk if your IdP allows arbitrary email assignment. Off by default.

Config.Name: PROXY_AUTH
Config.Description: Bypass first-party login and trust a forward-auth header (Authentik forward-auth, Authelia, oauth2-proxy). Hides /login. Requires PROXY_AUTH_SHARED_SECRET.

Config.Name: PROXY_AUTH_USER_HEADER
Config.Description: Header carrying the trusted username.

Config.Name: PROXY_AUTH_EMAIL_HEADER
Config.Description: Optional companion email header.

Config.Name: PROXY_AUTH_SHARED_SECRET
Config.Description: REQUIRED when PROXY_AUTH=true. The proxy must forward `X-Forward-Auth-Secret: <this>` on every request; mismatch → 401. Distinguishes proxy traffic from clients spoofing the username header.

Config.Name: PROXY_AUTH_TRUSTED_IPS
Config.Description: Comma-separated CIDRs allowed to send the trusted proxy-auth header, checked against the connecting socket peer. Only meaningful with PROXY_AUTH=true.

Config.Name: PROXY_AUTH_LOGOUT_URL
Config.Description: Where the sign-out button points in proxy mode (e.g. /outpost.goauthentik.io/sign_out for Authentik forward-auth). Unset → button hidden.
